newsitem.title: GERMANY: German printers step up industrial action.
newsitem.headline: German printers step up industrial action.

text.p: More than 20,000 workers at some 300 firms in the German printing industry have since the start of the week taken industrial action to protest against labour cost-cutting demanded by employers, union officials said on Wednesday.

IG Medien said that a further 4,000 workers out of the 130,000 employees in the sector had on Wednesday taken part in protest action ranging from one-hour walk-outs to downing tools for entire shifts.

Major German newspapers and printing groups, including the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung and the Axel Springer Verlag AG publishing group, have been hit by the stoppages, union officials said on Wednesday.
The protests went ahead as talks between IG Medien and employers in Frankfurt continued without signs of agreement over a new sector-wide wage agreement in the branch.
"So far we've just circled the area of conflict like cats around a hot pudding," IG Medien chief Detlef Hensche told reporters at the talks.

At issue is a 20 percent cut to sick pay entitlements made possible by a new federal law introduced late last year. Printing employers have told unions they are ready not to enforce the cuts, but as long as compensatory cost reductions can be agreed.

A spokesman for IG Medien said that if the talks broke up without agreement, it would then ballot its members on approval for full strikes. A minimum 75 percent of qualifying members must be in favour of strikes for them to go ahead.
